issues.legal_issue: The exception for culpable homicide arising from an act done while exceeding the right of private defence does not apply when no such right accrued.
material_facts: The deceased was unarmed when the appellant attacked him with an axe.
The High Court's observation that the appellant exceeded the limits of private defence was stray; the circumstances disclosed that no right of private defence of person or property had accrued.
issues.conclusion: The exception for exceeding the right of private defence did not apply, and it did not reduce the offence from murder.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 2 to Section 300 of the Penal Code presupposes that a right of private defence accrued and that the accused exceeded its limits; without an accrued right, the exception cannot apply. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and victim_unarmed and accused_attacked_victim and no_private_defence_right_accrued

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The case is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.victim_unarmed: The person attacked was not armed.
predicates.accused_attacked_victim: The accused used force against the person who died.
predicates.no_private_defence_right_accrued: The circumstances did not give the accused a right to defend a person or property.

issues.definition: When an appeal against a murder conviction concerns an attack on an unarmed person and no right to defend a person or property accrued to the accused, the exception for exceeding such a right does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: A sudden quarrel does not bring a killing within the sudden-fight exception when there was no bilateral exchange of blows and the accused inflicted multiple fatal blows with a formidable weapon on an unarmed victim.
material_facts: A quarrel broke out suddenly between the deceased's mother and the accused's companion.
The deceased was unarmed and did not injure the appellant or his companions.
The appellant inflicted three blows to the deceased's head with an axe, including one with its sharp side, and the deceased died at the scene.
issues.conclusion: The sudden-fight exception did not apply; the appellant's murder conviction was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Penal Code requires more than a sudden quarrel: there must be a sudden fight, which involves a bilateral transaction in which blows are exchanged. The judgment also considered that the deceased was unarmed and the appellant inflicted three fatal injuries with a formidable weapon. No earlier cases are relied on for this issue.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and sudden_quarrel and not blows_exchanged and victim_unarmed and multiple_fatal_weapon_blows

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The case is an appeal against a conviction for murder.
predicates.sudden_quarrel: A quarrel began suddenly before the fatal attack.
predicates.blows_exchanged: The accused and the victim both exchanged blows during the incident.
predicates.victim_unarmed: The person attacked was not armed.
predicates.multiple_fatal_weapon_blows: The accused inflicted multiple fatal blows on the victim with a formidable weapon.

issues.definition: When a murder-conviction appeal concerns a sudden quarrel but no exchange of blows, and the accused inflicted multiple fatal weapon blows on an unarmed victim, the sudden-fight exception does not apply.
